source.notes:
With the model code for blade heating system performance envelopes, IEA Task 54, an international
expert group for wind energy in cold climate, is proposing a simplified theoretical
model for simulating performance envelopes of an active blade heating system’s efficiency
for various operational boundaries. The model is based on python code and comes with an
executable file to provide a user-friendly interface.
For wind energy projects being developed and operated in cold climate conditions, an IPS
(Ice Protection System) - often including a blade heating system - can be required both due
to financial aspects as well as legal aspects. Production losses from icing can easily amount
to the largest fraction of losses for a wind farm in cold climate conditions. Thus, projection
and assessment of the performance of technical solutions designed to mitigate icing losses is
of high importance. As of today, there is limited available knowledge on how to select a wellfitting
system for a specific turbine as well as for a specific location. Hence, IEA Wind Task
54 provides a tool to model the performance according to turbine specifics and meteorological
conditions.
The purpose of the tool is for the end-user to model different blade heating system performance
envelopes to either project if a specific system would be a suitable choice for the respective
meteorological conditions of a project location, or to use on existing turbines with blade
heating system to evaluate the system’s performance and respective limits. As the complexity
of simulating all the phenomena for a rotating turbine blade in a natural environment with a
variety of thermodynamic effects is too advanced, the methodology of the presented model
is based on the assumption of keeping the blade ice-free and does not incorporate the actual
effect of ice build-up and melting. On the other hand, this reflects the goal of implementing a
blade heating system quite well.
source.title: Task 54 Blade heating Envelope model
